body: Polygon meshes of one adult male, based on whole-body MRI (the TARO voxel model) and refined/supplemented by medical illustrators (Mitsuhashi et al., 2009, Nucleic Acids Research 37:D782-5).
coordinates: BodyParts3D mm (x left, y posterior, z up) -> glTF (x, z, -y).
processing: Elements merged per node, decimated with quadric edge collapse (trimesh/fast-simplification); very low-poly parts (testes, bladder, amygdala, pineal) subdivided once or twice for smooth shading. Compressed with gltf-transform meshopt.

not_in_model.ovaries: The model is of a male body, so there are no ovaries. The lessons say this and mark their usual position with a dashed label only.

spinal_cord.label: Spinal cord
spinal_cord.approximate: BodyParts3D 4.0 has no spinal cord mesh. Drawn as a smooth tube through the centre of the real vertebral canal (found by ray casting each real vertebra), from the real medulla oblongata to the L1/L2 level, with typical adult widths.

thyroid.label: Thyroid gland
thyroid.approximate: BodyParts3D 4.0 has no thyroid gland. Drawn as two lobes joined by an isthmus, at typical adult size (lobes about 5 cm tall), wrapped around the real trachea just below the real cricoid cartilage, where the thyroid sits.

adrenal_medulla_left.label: Adrenal medulla (left)
adrenal_medulla_left.approximate: BodyParts3D 4.0 models the adrenal gland as one piece. The medulla is shown as the deepest central part of the real gland, about 10% of its volume (in life the medulla is roughly a tenth of the gland). The rest is the cortex.

diagrammatic_paths.leg_left: Sacral plexus and sciatic/tibial nerve: from the lower spinal nerves, in front of the real sacrum, out through the real greater sciatic notch, down behind the real femur and tibia to the sole of the foot.

animation_routes: Signal and blood routes for the animations follow these nerve paths and the centre lines of the real BodyParts3D vessels (found by 3D skeletonisation). Straight links join vessels where BodyParts3D has no mesh (for example the venous sinuses of the skull, the small thyroid veins and the lung capillaries).
